title: Autocomplete misses its keystroke budget
description: Your typeahead service holds a trie in memory. Each request walks the typed prefix's subtree to find the ten most popular completions. p50 is 4 ms, but p99 is 180 ms, mostly for one- and two-character prefixes. What would bring the slow tail within a 100 ms end-to-end budget?

options.text: Shard the trie by first letter so each server holds a smaller tree.
options.explanation: Short prefixes still walk large subtrees, and first-letter sharding creates hot shards for common letters.

options.text: Precompute and store the top-10 completions at every prefix node (or in a prefix-to-list map) at build time, so each request is a single lookup.
options.explanation: Do the ranking when building the index. Serving becomes one lookup regardless of how many completions share the prefix, so short prefixes no longer trigger huge subtree walks.

options.text: Move the trie into a relational database with an index on the query column.
options.explanation: A LIKE prefix scan plus sort on short prefixes touches millions of rows; it would be slower than the in-memory walk.

options.text: Increase the client debounce to 500 ms so fewer requests are sent.
options.explanation: Fewer requests reduce load but make suggestions feel laggy and do nothing about slow server-side lookups for short prefixes.
